title: Reified RSpaces P1: Rust items of the storage substrate, the fix rules FR-1 to FR-9, the round-2 rules FR-1', FR-5', FR-7' and FR-9' the round-3 rule FR-10 and decision 36 (replay reproduces play), and the formal models that cover them
design: p1-design-report §5(a), plan decision 19 (D1-D7), P1 fix rules FR-1 to FR-9, the round-2 rules FR-1', FR-5', FR-7' and FR-9' and the round-3 rule FR-10 (prompts/p1-fix-rules.md, plan decision 30), and decision 36 (it amends decision 19: an unpaired replay fire stages and fails at commit)
code_base: The host code that the models cite is the campaign tree after the merge of feature/cost-accounted-rho at 4d67b5ccc (HEAD 6f7a80da3 before the merge). The P1 items are in new files. The line numbers below are informative. The checker finds each item by its scope and name. An item with "status": "pending" is code that another change still writes.

H1.name: commit_trace_eq_host
H1.statement: A commit makes the same observer calls, events and status as the host run of the same operations.

H2.name: commit_state_eq_host
H2.statement: A commit leaves the same store as the host run (data lists up to permutation).

H3.name: counter_timing_play_replay
H3.statement: The play counter closure gives the same COMM counts as the replay increment-first rule.

H4.name: verify_sound_complete
H4.statement: verify looks up only the trigger key of the fire (FR-3). It pairs a COMM exactly when the log holds the trigger event and an unpaired recorded occurrence remains, and recorded_comms reports the same copies. Decision 36: a fire whose log lacks the trigger event stages unpaired, with no pairing and no binding change, and an unpaired fire never commits: it emits no event or effect and leaves the bindings and the store. The any-key rule before FR-3 and the literal design rule both over-pair.

H5.name: replay_pairs_each_comm_once
H5.statement: Replay pairs every recorded COMM occurrence at most once.

H6.name: view_commit_coherent
H6.statement: The staged view equals the committed store.

H7.name: joins_lockstep_preserved
H7.statement: The join entries stay in lockstep with the waiting continuations.

H8.name: sub_order_between
H8.statement: Sub-orders follow the parent order, precede its successors, and are contiguous and unique.

H9.name: abort_inert
H9.statement: A drop, an access error and a commit after a store swap change no store, binding, observer call, event or generation. The reads of the aborted session stay cached, but FR-1 admits only fresh canonical keys, so the checkpoint succeeds with the same history map.

H10.name: coverage_total
H10.statement: Every store change of a commit has its event.

H11.name: peek_reproduces_trace_eq_host
H11.statement: FR-10 and decision 45 (Rule E): a staged transaction with the re-stores of a consume-side peek fire right after the fire commits with the observer calls, events, status and bindings of the host run in which the reducer's produce_peeks sends the removed records again, and the stores are equal (data up to permutation). A committed fire never stores a datum, the receipt carries the stored persist flags, a fire removes its stored non-persistent records in the view also for a peek, the re-stores are exactly HEAD's produce_peeks, each re-store has the identity of the removed record and is a staged Store, and a peek fire with its re-stores keeps every data list up to permutation. After a produce-side fire, HEAD's re-produces are the re-offer of the incoming datum plus the re-stores. The decision 30 re-offer conjuncts are unchanged.

H12.name: reporting_trace_is_replay_trace
H12.statement: The reporting mode stages and commits as the replay mode does.

H13.name: sweep_exact
H13.statement: The sweep removes exactly the data, continuations and joins of the volatile channels. Through the handle, a sweep in a context that holds an open transaction of the same handle fails closed with NestedTransaction and leaves the store as it was (FR-9'). In any other context the handle runs exactly this sweep.

H14.name: delete_absent_identity
H14.statement: A history delete of an absent key changes nothing, in make_actions and in the duplicate-checking checkpoint.

H15.name: sweep_root_neutral
H15.statement: Under FR-1 (canonical cache keys and canonical sweep groups) and collision-free history keys, the checkpoint after the sweep succeeds, and its trie is the trie of the durable changes alone. The checkpoint model rejects two actions on one key.

H16.name: leaf_count_is_length
H16.statement: After a successful checkpoint, the root leaf record count is the length of the data list.

H17.name: non_canonical_fails_closed
H17.statement: FR-1': a group that is not non-decreasing fails with NonCanonicalChannelOrder, and a non-decreasing group passes, also when it repeats a channel. Each permutation class has exactly one member that passes, its sorted list. A non-canonical read or stage fails before any store or cache effect, every access caches only fresh canonical keys, and a successful session stages exactly the operations of stage_all, each with canonical groups.

H18.name: canonical_reads_root_neutral
H18.statement: A non-canonical read fails. Reads of canonical keys change no stored list, keep the cache duplicate free, canonical and read-through, and leave the checkpoint trie with the same leaf at every history key, so the root is unchanged.

H19.name: directive_fails_closed
H19.statement: In replay and reporting, a replay directive at the directive position rejects the operation with no store, binding, event or effect change, and the commit stops there. The host would go native instead.

H20.name: parent_order_single_txn
H20.statement: FR-5 and FR-5': sub_order is injective. A second commit under one parent in one evaluation scope fails before any effect. A scope reset (begin_evaluation_scope), a store swap and a session change each reset the tracker. Every run of commits in one scope emits pairwise distinct sub-orders of fresh parents. Two evaluations of one deploy that a reset separates both commit under the same parent path, and without a reset the second commit fails.

H21.name: view_identity_is_store_identity
H21.statement: FR-2: view lookups and the installed guard respect store identity, the staged view agrees with the committed store after the same writes, and an Ord-keyed view disagrees for two channels with one store identity.

H22.name: checkpoint_rejects_duplicate_key_actions
H22.statement: The checkpoint refuses two actions on one history key, as RadixHistory::process does. Two cached permutations of one group, or a read of a permuted key next to its cached group, make the checkpoint fail. Under FR-1' the sorted list is the unique canonical member of its permutation class, also when a group repeats a channel. So with collision freedom up to order the canonical cache keys have distinct history keys (key_injective).

H23.name: replay_reproduces_play_run
H23.statement: Decision 36: play and replay stage the same operations from the same view. When the bindings of replay hold the IO events and the COMMs that play commits (the commit log of play), replay stages exactly the operations of play, and its commit makes the observer calls of play (directive queries erased), the events, the status and the store of play. An operation that play rejects (an out-of-phlo charge) fails replay at the same call after the same prefix.

T1.name: ReplayPrefixEqual
T1.statement: The replay log is a prefix of the play log, and equals it when the replay completes.

T2.name: SameRootIffSameState
T2.statement: Two checkpoints have the same root exactly when they have the same hot store state.

T3.name: PairedOnce
T3.statement: Replay pairs a COMM at most as often as the play log records it.

T4.name: NoVolatileResidue
T4.statement: No history trie holds a volatile channel.

T5.name: Serializable
T5.statement: With FR-4 lock coverage, every interleaving of space transactions and host operations equals a serial order of the committed units, also for groups that repeat a channel (FR-1'). UncoveredChannelUnsafe and UnjoinedChannelUnsafe refute it.

T6.name: ReplayOutcomeEqual
T6.statement: Decision 36: an honest block (its log is the commit log of play) is never rejected, and its replayed deploy ends with the failure and the spending of play, also when the deploy runs out of phlo inside a transaction.

FR-3.title: Trigger-key replay pairing
FR-3.note: Decision 36 (it amends decision 19) keeps the trigger-key rule and changes only the consequence of no pairing: the fire stages unpaired and fails at commit after the calls of play (StagedFire.recorded, StagedConsumeFire.recorded, ReplayBackend::produce_fire and consume_observed; H4, H23, T6).

FR-5'.title: Parent tracking per root evaluation scope (round 2)

FR-7'.title: Always-on checks cost O(changed entries) (round 2)
FR-7'.note: The checks now inspect only the entries that an operation changes. Their decisions and failure semantics (Inconsistent, EventCoverage) are unchanged, so the model is unchanged.

FR-8.title: Sweep bookkeeping
FR-8.unmodeled: The counts and the replay estimate have no store effect. H13 covers the removals.

FR-9.title: Nested begin
FR-9.unmodeled: A guard at begin with no store effect. It is outside the Rocq and TLA+ models.

FR-9'.title: The sweep honors the nested-transaction guard (round 2)

FR-10.title: Peek fires re-offer the sent value (round 3)
FR-10.supersedes: The storing of the incoming datum of a produce-side peek fire (P1 §6, plan decision 19).

items.name: stage_produce
items.role: Stages one produce: lock coverage of the channel (phase A), the fired group (admit_group), the join channels (phase B), then the view loads, the trigger-key pairing and the view effects (design §1.4, FR-1, FR-3, FR-4).

items.name: stage_consume
items.role: Stages one consume: admit_group (arity, canonical order, lock coverage in both phases, installed guard) before any hot-store access, then fire against stored data or park the continuation and its joins (FR-1, FR-4).

items.name: verify
items.role: Replay pairing under the trigger key only (FR-3): Produce(source) for a produce-side fire, Consume(source) for a consume-side fire. The COMM pairs while paired < count / binding_multiplicity. Decision 36: it returns the recorded COMM or None and never fails, so an unpaired fire stages as in play and replay staging equals play staging.

items.name: StagedFire
items.role: A staged produce-side fire. Its field recorded holds the recorded COMM that the fire paired with in replay and reporting, and None in play and for an unpaired replay fire (decision 36).

items.name: StagedConsumeFire
items.role: A staged consume-side fire. Decision 36 adds its field recorded, with the meaning of StagedFire.recorded.

items.name: binding_multiplicity
items.role: The bindings that one recorded COMM occurrence adds under a key in rig.

items.name: apply_op
items.role: Commits one staged operation through the host play call sequence (design §2.1).

items.name: produce_fire
items.role: The play commit of a produce-side fire (source, persist, fire). It runs observe_comm, log_produce and log_comm, then removes the continuation, the stored non-persistent records and the fired joins, also for a peek fire (decision 45). FR-10: it never stores the incoming datum. It returns fired_receipt with the flags of the host.

items.name: apply_op
items.role: Commits one staged operation through the host replay call sequence (design §2.2) and removes the bindings of each pairing.

items.name: produce_fire
items.role: The replay commit of a produce-side fire: the play effects with the replay continuation estimate and remove_bindings_for. Decision 36: after observe_comm accepts, an unpaired fire (recorded = None) fails with ReplayDivergence before it logs, removes or unbinds anything. FR-10: it never stores the incoming datum. Decision 45: it removes the stored non-persistent records also for a peek fire. It returns fired_receipt with the flags of the host.

items.name: produce_observed
items.role: The replay commit of a produce after its call prefix: it refuses a directive, observes the introduction, steps the counter, then stores or fires. A failed fire, also an unpaired one, rolls the counter step back (decision 36).

items.name: consume_observed
items.role: The replay commit of a consume after its call prefix: park, or fire. Decision 36: after observe_comm accepts, an unpaired fire (recorded = None) fails with ReplayDivergence before it logs, removes or unbinds anything.

items.name: begin
items.role: The reporting mode: begin_replay with SpaceMode::Reporting, so apply_op is ReplayBackend::apply_op (design §2.3).

items.name: begin_replay
items.role: Opens a replay or reporting transaction over ReplayBackend.

items.name: commit_staged
items.role: Applies the staged operations in order under sub_order(parent, i). StoreSwapped rejects the commit before any operation, and TxnRegistration::admit_parent rejects a second commit under one parent (FR-5). A failure of operation i keeps operations 0..i (decision D6). Decision 36: an unpaired replay fire fails here, with the error of a rejected call or with ReplayDivergence, and with the same prefix.

items.name: commit_operation
items.role: Commits one staged operation: apply_op applies it, after the state check of the entries that it removes (ready_produce, ready_consume), and then the event correlation is checked. Both checks cost O(changed entries) and run in every build profile, so debug and release commit identical results (FR-7').

items.name: commit
items.role: Closes the transaction, clears the staged pairings and the counter delta, commits the staged operations and releases the locks and the registration.

items.name: TxnView
items.role: The staged view overlay with the counter delta (design §1.3). Every map is keyed by the store identity (FR-2).

items.name: check_event_correlation
items.role: Correlates the staged effects of one operation with the events that its commit emits, in every build profile (FR-7, FR-7'). By H6 the staged effects are the effects of the commit, so H10 shows that the check never fails for a staged transaction.

items.name: sub_order
items.role: The order of operation i of a transaction: parent.path ++ [(i, SUB_OPERATION_TAG)] (decision D3).

items.name: SUB_OPERATION_TAG
items.role: The path tag 2 of a sub-order. ReductionContext uses 0 and 1.

items.name: sweep_volatile_channels
items.role: The volatile sweep of every host mode (design §3.1): validation (installed guard, require_canonical on every stored join group, crossing groups, persisted keys) before any mutation, the continuation, join and data loops, and the post check. SweepReport.joins counts the joins actually removed, and on_continuation_removed lets the replay host update its estimate (FR-8).

items.name: sweep_volatile
items.role: The play host sweep: consume_lock on the swept channels, the history reader at the current root, then sweep_volatile_channels.

items.name: sweep_volatile
items.role: The replay host sweep through sweep_replay.

items.name: sweep_volatile
items.role: The reporting host sweep: sweep_replay over the inner replay space.

items.name: sweep_volatile
items.role: Runs the sweep of the host through the handle. It fails closed with NestedTransaction, before any lock or hot-store access, when the current task holds an open transaction of this handle (FR-9').

items.name: root_leaf_records
items.role: The record count of the data leaf of a channel at a history root (the outer frame, decision D5).

items.name: root_leaf_record_count
items.role: The play host count at the current history root.

items.name: root_leaf_record_count
items.role: The replay host count through replay_root_leaf_record_count.

items.name: root_leaf_record_count
items.role: The reporting host count over the inner replay space.

items.name: root_leaf_record_count
items.role: The handle entry point. It delegates to the host.

items.name: require_canonical
items.role: Admits a group whose channel keys are non-decreasing (FR-1'). A group can repeat a channel. Any other order fails with NonCanonicalChannelOrder. One channel is always canonical.

items.name: canonical_group_key
items.role: FR-1: the key of a non-empty canonical group (group_identity, then require_canonical). Every staged group and every continuations read goes through it.

items.name: admit_group
items.role: FR-1 and FR-4: arity, canonical order, lock coverage and the installed guard of a staged group, in that order and before any hot-store access.

items.name: read_continuations
items.role: FR-1: SpaceTxn::continuations checks the canonical group key before the hot-store read.

items.name: read_joins
items.role: FR-1: SpaceTxn::joins loads the joins key of the channel, then checks each returned group.

items.name: load_joins
items.role: Loads the join groups of a channel through the hot store and rejects a non-canonical stored group (FR-1).

items.name: NonCanonicalChannelOrder
items.role: FR-1': a channel group is not sorted (non-decreasing) by channel hash, so a decreasing pair exists (also a non-canonical stored join group in a sweep). A repeated channel is canonical.

items.name: channel_key
items.role: FR-2: the store identity of a channel, stable_hash_provider::hash(channel), the key of every substrate map and set.

items.name: group_identity
items.role: FR-2: the store identity of a group, its channel keys in group order.

items.name: installed_channels
items.role: FR-2: the installed-channel guard set, keyed by store identity.

items.name: recorded_comms
items.role: FR-3: the recorded COMMs under the trigger key of the queried source that this transaction has not paired: count / binding_multiplicity minus the paired copies.

items.name: ReplayDivergence
items.role: FR-3 and decision 36: an unpaired replay fire, whose trigger event holds no free recorded occurrence of its COMM. Commit raises it after the observer accepts every call of the fire, and the operations before it stay applied (D6).

items.name: LockCoverage
items.role: FR-4: the exact stripes that begin holds, in phase A and phase B.

items.name: new
items.role: FR-4: records the stripes of the lock keys for both phases, as striped_locks::consume_lock takes them.

items.name: require
items.role: FR-4: a touched channel must have its stripe in the phase that the host uses for it (Produced: phase A, Joined: phase B, Consumed: both). Otherwise staging fails with UnlockedChannel.

items.name: holds
items.role: FR-4: membership of a channel hash in the held stripes of one phase.

items.name: LockUse
items.role: FR-4: how the host locks a touched channel: Produced, Joined or Consumed.

items.name: UnlockedChannel
items.role: FR-4: the transaction does not hold the stripe of a touched channel in the phase that the host uses for it.

items.name: admit
items.role: Admits one commit per parent order in the current evaluation scope (FR-5). A commit with another session or another store Arc resets the tracker first (FR-5').

items.name: begin_evaluation_scope
items.role: Resets the tracker of committed parents at the start of a root evaluation (FR-5'). P4 calls it at the entry of ReducerCore::inj_with_observation and inj, in play and in replay.

items.name: admit_parent
items.role: FR-5: commit_staged admits the parent order after the StoreSwapped check and before any operation.

items.name: HandleState
items.role: The state that the clones of a handle share: the contexts with an open transaction (FR-9, FR-9') and the tracker of committed parents (FR-5, FR-5').

items.name: ParentOrderReused
items.role: FR-5: a transaction already committed under the current parent operation order.

items.name: counter_room
items.role: FR-6: checked room for one more produce counter increment before any effect.

items.name: staged_count
items.role: FR-6: the staged counter host + delta with checked arithmetic.

items.name: next_delta
items.role: FR-6: the staged increment of a non-persistent produce with checked arithmetic.

items.name: CounterOverflow
items.role: FR-6: a produce counter would exceed i32::MAX. The operation fails before any effect.

items.name: check_removed_records
items.role: The state check of FR-7 and FR-7': before any effect of an operation, each record that it removes sits at the position where the staged view held it (Inconsistent otherwise). It costs O(changed entries) and runs in every build profile.

items.name: SweepReport
items.role: FR-8: the sweep counts. joins counts the joins actually removed.
items.unmodeled: FR-8 bookkeeping has no store effect. sweep_volatile_channels (H13) carries the removals that it counts.

items.name: register
items.role: FR-9: begin fails closed with NestedTransaction before it takes any lock when the current task already holds an open transaction of the handle.
items.unmodeled: FR-9 is a guard at begin with no store effect. The Rocq lifecycle and the TLA+ model have at most one open transaction for each actor. The FR-9' guard of the sweep is modeled (handle_sweep, H13).

items.name: TxnContext
items.role: The execution context of an open transaction: the tokio task, or the thread without a task.

items.name: NestedTransaction
items.role: FR-9: the current task already holds an open transaction of this handle.

items.name: reject_directive
items.role: Spaces fail closed on a replay directive (decision 19 D4): NativeReplayDirectiveUnsupported before any effect of the operation.

items.name: NativeReplayDirectiveUnsupported
items.role: The observer returned a native replay directive. The operation fails closed (H19).

items.name: apply_fire_to_view
items.role: The view effects of a produce-side fire: the continuation removal, the removed records and the fired joins. FR-10 removed its key and incoming parameters, so it never stores the incoming datum.

items.name: check_peeks
items.role: The peeks rule of a fire: no peeks, or every bind. Any other peek set is MixedArrowJoin. It decides nothing about the removal, because every fire removes its stored non-persistent records (decision 45, Rule E).

items.name: removed_records
items.role: The stored records that a fire removes: the non-persistent stored candidates, also for a peek fire (decision 45, Rule E). The incoming datum is never a removed record.

items.name: fired_receipt
items.role: fired_receipt(comm, wrapped, candidates, produce) builds the receipt of a fire from the host's wrap_result. Every result keeps the persist flag of the host (decision 45, Rule E), so a non-persistent result tells the agent that the fire removed or spent its datum. The commit fails with Inconsistent when the result count differs from the candidates.
